consumer_audit.evidence: index_engine.cpp:1671-1688 CommitMappedFile publishes aggregate; 2507/2525-2528 merge, 3269/3286-3288 single-volume rebuild, 3412/3439-3443 initial build publish aggregate then derive volume shards. TryLoadCache:2566-2574 imports validated legacy pulse-index.bin into aggregate; this import does not make aggregate itself obsolete.

TryLoadCache:2544-2583 resolves active/previous aggregate and adopts its map. AdoptMappedLocked:1885-1933 creates canonical global nodes and per-volume FRN/journal/USN state from it. OpenDeltasLocked/ReplayDeltasLocked:2200-2264 attach updates to this generation. RebuildVolumeMft:3172-3198 flattens the current canonical view, preserves healthy volumes and replaces the failed volume before publishing a new aggregate. No audited path reconstructs this canonical state from per-volume query copies.

WriteVolumeShards:1713-1762 serializes Node/Attr/name/FRN slices from the already-built aggregate; invoked after successful initial build, merge and single-volume rebuild. These are derived copies of the same dataset, not another scanner.

RefreshQueryShardsLocked:1936-1969 requires an existing aggregate map and matching built time, node count and volume ID for every volume; maps all volumes while retaining aggregate. QueryShardForLocked/QueryNodeAtLocked/QueryAttrAtLocked/QueryNameOfLocked:1972-2002 convert local IDs and fall back to aggregate accessors. CollectMatchesLocked:989-994 selects one posting source. SortIdsLocked:1126-1195 contains optional per-volume ordered-stream merge; current WriteIndexFile:1552-1554 omits those three ordering arrays, so that stream shortcut is unavailable for newly written current snapshots. Query output/authorization use the same canonical global IDs. Memory diagnostics:379 only account for mapped copies.

index_delta.cpp:63-73 writes live per-volume delta WAL under root/Volumes/<volume-hash>/wal-a.log. This root-level Volumes tree is distinct from v9/volumes query snapshots. A future query-copy optimization must not disable or delete live delta logs.

storage_contract_assessment.why_per_volume_exists: The introducing commit 7640746 describes pending index shards but supplies no verified design rationale or benchmark. Current code establishes a per-volume query layout with locally numbered nodes/postings and optional sorted-stream machinery. It does not establish an OOM requirement: all volume maps and the aggregate remain mapped together. Any locality/performance benefit remains a hypothesis until measured.
storage_contract_assessment.fallback_contract: Aggregate query fallback is a normal production branch, not solely an error handler: helper scope never uses per-volume maps; machine initial build marks the aggregate ready before writing volume copies; absent, mismatched or unreadable volume query shards leave query_shards_ready_ false. Posting collection, query accessors, ranking, path reconstruction and general sorting have aggregate paths. This is strong static support for a simpler mode, but not a completed parity proof for disabling the feature.

minimal_candidate.direction: Retain aggregate as authoritative snapshot and retain its A/B recovery contract. Make per-volume query-copy generation and loading consistently optional; initially evaluate with the option disabled against the existing aggregate path.
code_points: index_engine.cpp:1713 WriteVolumeShards: single policy guard avoids its three callers generating new query-copy snapshots.
index_engine.cpp:1936 RefreshQueryShardsLocked: after clearing maps/ready flag, the same policy guard returns before loading old copies.
Keep canonical aggregate publish/adoption, query IDs, live root-level Volumes WAL, USN processing, per-volume recovery and caller visibility unchanged.
minimal_candidate.existing_data: Stopping writes does not reclaim existing v9/volumes bytes. Any later cleanup requires a separate verified migration: validate active/previous aggregate, exclude live mappings/writers and only remove inventory-proven derived query copies. No deletion or cleanup is authorized/performed in this audit.
minimal_candidate.expected_benefit: Eliminates a second newly serialized snapshot set and associated temporary store/posting work. The user-observed equal directory totals suggest this set is material, but actual allocated-space savings and latency changes were not measured; no promise of matching Everything size.
minimal_candidate.risk: Cold/warm query page locality and tail latency can change, particularly cross-volume or restricted-path searches; aggregate still spans the full dataset. Startup checksum/mmap, paging, peak private memory and commit I/O must be compared. Removing aggregate instead requires a larger canonical-state/FRN/WAL/startup redesign and is not the minimal option.
minimal_candidate.decision: Do not implement during this read-only turn. The minimal direction appears feasible from code, but full functional and performance equivalence is unverified and existing-space reclamation needs its own safe migration contract. Leave the choice for the next interaction without further questions now.

reuse_without_full_suite: pulse_index_engine_test --cache-resolution-only: active CRC/manifest failures, legacy import and two-slot rebuild publication.
--shard-recovery-only and --shard-io-rebuild-only: exact A/B fallback and I/O failure preservation.
--outstanding-query-only / --outstanding-structure-only / --query-narrowing-only: hit sets, path reconstruction, rename/move, scoped queries, dense/sparse and pagination boundaries.
--delta-replay-only / --mixed-usn-only / --feed-only / --authorization-only: canonical updates, query-visible revisions and caller scope.
focused_validation_for_a_future_change.missing_comparison: Existing selectors are useful but are not a dedicated per-volume-enabled versus disabled parity suite. Add one isolated identical multi-volume synthetic dataset comparison for name/path/kind/size/time filters, ranking, ascending/descending sorting, offsets, rapid cancellation, rename/delete overlays, offline/returning volumes and restart/WAL recovery; no real user volume mutations.
focused_validation_for_a_future_change.performance: Compare cold/warm first-page and tail latency, service startup, merge write bytes, resident/private/peak memory and total logical/allocated snapshot bytes on the same dataset. Existing index_perf_main.cpp queries the default service pipe and is not an isolated paired harness; adapt a private comparison rather than automatically benchmarking the live service.
